business_problem: BBVA needed to help customers manage spending, savings, investments, and future outgoings with personalized guidance, while also coping with inconsistent transaction data from other banks that was too sparse for simple rule-based categorization.
solution_summary: BBVA built an AI-driven financial health workflow around its BBVA app and transactional website to turn raw banking activity into personalized guidance. The serving layer is the customer-facing app, website, and Budgets experience, where users see categorized spending, savings and investment views, forward-looking cash-flow estimates, and alerts. Upstream, BBVA ingests account and card transactions from its own systems plus aggregated transaction records from other banks when customers request it, along with comments left inside the financial health features. Compute is split by data quality: deterministic algorithms classify richly described BBVA transactions in real time, while a neural network model using NLP infers categories from sparse external-bank descriptions. BBVA also uses advanced analytics for segmentation, language models to mine feedback themes, ensemble machine learning to forecast recurring transactions, and an account balance prediction model to flag deviations. The source does not name a separate storage platform.

solution_components.name: BBVA app
solution_components.role: Serves categorized transactions, forecasts, balance expectations, and alerts to customers.

solution_components.name: transactional website
solution_components.role: Provides the same financial health experiences and transaction views through BBVA's web channel.

solution_components.name: Budgets
solution_components.role: Is surfaced to customer segments that need help making ends meet.

solution_components.name: neural network model
solution_components.role: Infers categories for aggregated transactions from other banks using transaction descriptions and other limited fields.

solution_components.name: language models
solution_components.role: Extract positive and negative themes from customer comments to improve financial health proposals.

solution_components.name: ensemble machine learning
solution_components.role: Predicts future transactions, expected amounts, and dates by combining multiple models.

solution_components.name: account balance prediction model
solution_components.role: Uses a neural network to forecast balance evolution and detect out-of-the-ordinary values.

data_flow: BBVA pulls account and card transactions from its own banking systems and, when authorized, aggregated transaction data from other banks into classification pipelines. Deterministic rules process detailed BBVA records, while a neural network with NLP interprets sparse external descriptions. The resulting categories, forecasts, segments, and anomaly signals are served through the BBVA app, transactional website, and Budgets tools, where customer edits and comments feed back into model improvement.
integration_points: BBVA account and card transaction systems
Aggregated transaction data from other banks
Customer comments submitted within BBVA financial health features
business_outcome: BBVA increased engagement with its digital financial health features and improved customer satisfaction by providing real-time transaction categorization, more tailored financial proposals, forward-looking expense forecasts, and alerts on unusual bills or balance deviations.
metrics: six out of ten digital users leverage these features
satisfaction rates nearly 24% higher than non-digital users
70 million times in Q1 2024, a 23 percent year-over-year increase
391 million interactions with these features across all the countries where BBVA is present, 49% more than in the same period in 2023
architecture_clues: Since June 2023, in Spain, credit card transactions are classified in real time.
Manual reclassifications by customers also apply instantly.
Other-bank transaction records are typically limited to bank identifier, transaction type, amount, and a variable description.
Forecasts cover the current month and the next month.
The account balance prediction model generates predictions at different probability levels and supports long-term predictions that reflect expected variability.
